findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: The class subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and its body is just `pass`. This PR adds a new `@abc.abstractmethod` `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and the existing abstract methods `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value` and `get_group_key_values` are also not implemented. Instantiating the class therefore raises TypeError. `Detector.detector_handler` constructs the handler for every detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, so `process_detectors` will crash for those detectors. Previously the handler's `evaluate` returned [] and worked. Either keep a non-abstract placeholder implementation or implement the required methods.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the signature now returns a dict keyed by group key. Callers and readers relying on the docstring will expect the wrong type.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores the value it is supposed to report
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` never uses its `value` argument, and the occurrence does not depend on it. Several tests build the expected occurrence with value 6 while evaluating a different value (e.g. `test_results_on_change` evaluates 100, `test_dedupe` evaluates 8). Because the expected and actual occurrences are built the same way, these assertions cannot detect the hook being called with the wrong value or group key. The new hook's argument contract is therefore not actually tested.
